extracted.intended_audience: FAA rulewriters, aviation stakeholders (pilots, airport operators), and regulatory/legal practitioners involved in airspace rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and publishing an FAA final rule that amends the legal description of Class D airspace for a specific airport (here, Republic Airport, Farmingdale, NY), including required statutory authority, incorporation by reference, explanatory preamble, and administrative amendments. Covers both the technical content of the airspace description and the procedural/legal justifications (e.g., bypassing notice-and-comment, regulatory and environmental analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking must identify the FAA's statutory authority under Title 49 of the United States Code (e.g., Subtitle I, Section 106; Subtitle VII, Section 40103) and cite any relevant Executive Orders or statutory provisions authorizing the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document states the FAA's authority to issue rules regarding aviation safety is found in Title 49 U.S.C.; specifies Subtitle VII, Part A, Subpart I, Section 40103 as the charge to prescribe regulations to assign airspace for safety and efficient use. The authority citation for 14 CFR part 71 must continue to read with the listed U.S.C. sections and E.O. citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials (e.g., FAA Order JO 7400.11) that are incorporated by reference must be identified (title, edition), the legal basis cited (1 CFR part 51), and the incorporation approved by the Director of the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document amends the current version of FAA Order JO 7400.11K (dated August 4, 2025). Incorporation by reference is done under 1 CFR part 51 on an annual basis; the Director of the Federal Register approves incorporation actions and such amendments will be published in the next update to FAA Order JO 7400.11. Provide public availability information in the ADDRESSES section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of airspace legal description
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal description of a Class D airspace area must state the airport name, geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude), vertical limits (surface up to specified MSL), lateral dimensions (radius(es), bearings, and sectors), and effective times/conditions for the airspace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'Republic Airport, NY (Lat. 40°43′45" N, long. 73°24′48" W). That airspace extending upward from the surface to and including 2,600 feet MSL within a 4.2-mile radius of Republic Airport extending clockwise from the 065° bearing to the 270° bearing and within a 5.3-mile radius ... extending clockwise from the 270° to the 065° bearing ... effective during the times and dates established in advance by a Notice to Airmen. The date and time will thereafter be continuously published in the Chart Supplement.' Ensure the legal description makes clear whether boundaries or operating requirements are changed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of current FAA publications and references
rubrics_metrics.description: References in legal descriptions should use the currently authorized FAA publication names and the appropriate publication where effective times and details will be published (e.g., replace 'Airport/Facility Directory' with 'Chart Supplement').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action replaces the reference to 'Airport/Facility Directory' with 'Chart Supplement' to comply with current FAA policy. State where dates/times will be published (Chart Supplement) and ensure cross-references conform to current FAA nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause for bypassing notice-and-comment
rubrics_metrics.description: To issue a final rule without prior notice and comment, the agency must make a 'good cause' finding under 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(B) that notice-and-comment is impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest, and explain the reasons in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule invokes good cause because the amendment is 'an administrative change' that is 'routine, insignificant in nature and impact, and inconsequential to the industry and to the public.' Support the finding with precedent and guidance (e.g., Mack Trucks, Inc. v. EPA; Utility Solid Waste Activities Group v. EPA; Attorney General's Manual on the APA; DOT Order 2100.6B) and explain why the change does not impose substantive restrictions that would make notice useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory notices and analyses criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the rule is a 'significant regulatory action' under Executive Order 12866, a 'significant rule' under DOT policies, and whether a regulatory evaluation is required; assess impacts under the Regulatory Flexibility Act for small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAA determined this regulation: (1) is not a significant regulatory action under EO 12866; (2) is not a significant rule under DOT Regulatory Policies and Procedures; and (3) does not warrant preparation of a regulatory evaluation because anticipated impact is minimal. Certify whether the rule will have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities under the RFA and document the rationale when impacts are minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental review and categorical exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the action qualifies for a categorical exclusion under NEPA in accordance with FAA environmental procedures (e.g., FAA Order 1050.1G), and document that no extraordinary circumstances exist requiring an environmental assessment or EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This action qualified for categorical exclusion under FAA Order 1050.1G paragraph B-2.5(a). Explain that the airspace action is not expected to cause any potentially significant environmental impacts and state that no extraordinary circumstances exist that would warrant further NEPA analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preamble content and administrative explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The preamble to the final rule should explain the reason for the amendment, describe the changes (e.g., administrative updates to coordinates and publications), and state whether boundaries or operating requirements are affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a SUMMARY that concisely states the action, a SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section with 'Authority for This Rulemaking', 'Incorporation by Reference', 'The Rule', and any 'Good Cause' or other procedural justifications. Explicitly state that changes are ministerial when appropriate and explain operational impact (or lack thereof).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and publication metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rule documents should include agency name, action type, docket and airspace docket numbers, CFR part(s) affected, RIN, document citation (FR volume and page), document number, pages, publication and effective dates, and contact information for further inquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document lists: Department/Agency, 14 CFR Part 71, Docket No. FAA-2026-2421; Airspace Docket No. 26-AEA-4; RIN 2120-AA66; Document Citation 91 FR 9982; Document Number 2026-04082; Effective date 0901 UTC, July 9, 2026; FOR FURTHER INFORMATION CONTACT with name, group, address, and phone. Include ADDRESSES for viewing the rule and background (e.g., regulations.gov, federalregister.gov, FAA publications). See the Document Drafting Handbook for details on headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket availability and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information on where the final rule and background material can be accessed (e.g., Regulations.gov docket, FederalRegister.gov, FAA publications) and whether supporting documents are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the docket number for electronic retrieval (available 24/7 at regulations.gov), provide electronic download links (federalregister.gov), and list availability of FAA orders (e.g., FAA Order JO 7400.11K). If no supporting documents are available, state that explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and Director approval language
rubrics_metrics.description: State the effective date and include language that the Director of the Federal Register approves incorporation by reference actions under 1 CFR part 51, subject to annual revisions and publication of conforming amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This document sets Effective date 0901 UTC, July 9, 2026 and states: 'The Director of the Federal Register approves this incorporation by reference action under 1 CFR part 51, subject to the annual revision of FAA Order JO 7400.11 and publication of conforming amendments.' Include such approval language when incorporating FAA orders.
